GitHub: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/437#issuecomment-5575662594

Reproduced a remaining regression in **pm-cli 2026.9.7** on Linux / Node 22.20.0, with `--no-extensions` on every command. Reusing this closed canonical issue after searching all issue states for `claim receipt`, `claim output`, and `claim compact` and reviewing #195 and #437.

In a fresh temporary working directory:

```bash
export PM_AUTHOR=claim-output-repro
pm init probe --json --no-extensions
pm create Task 'Mutation output reproduction' --id probe-claim \
  --description 'Reproduce claim output without custom extensions' \
  --status open --priority 2 --create-mode progressive --json --no-extensions
pm claim probe-claim --json --no-extensions
```

`create` emits the documented flat `{id, status, changed_field_count}` receipt (75 bytes in this reproduction). `claim` instead emits `{item, claimed_by, previous_assignee, forced}` with the full item (550 bytes even for this tiny fixture), no top-level `id` or `status`, and no `changed_field_count`. Claiming a populated real project epic repeats its description and complete comments, making the discrepancy substantially larger.

The current root `--help` says mutations emit a flat receipt, so callers following that documented contract cannot parse `claim` like `create`/`update`. Output projection is not a workaround: `claim --output-include item.id,item.status` correctly rejects read-only output controls.

Please include `claim` in the default compact mutation contract, retaining claim-specific outcome/ownership fields where necessary and an explicit full-output opt-in. This is reproducible without project custom extensions; no extension issue is implicated.


Current-checkout verification: isolated no-extension CLI create emits 71 bytes with id/status/changed_field_count; claim emits 517 bytes with item/claimed_by/previous_assignee/forced and no top-level id/status/change count. Synthetic fixture only.
Claim ownership response repeats full metadata despite the compact mutation contract
Apply compact mutation receipt projection to claim while preserving ownership outcomes, contention semantics and explicit full output.

Default claim exposes compact item identity and status with truthful change count and required ownership outcomes; explicit full output and id-only/quiet precedence remain compatible; preserve contention and no-op/refusal behavior; validate CLI/MCP/SDK parity and bounded output for metadata-rich items using real installed consumers.

value.text: Duplicate check: a strict full read of all 2656 items across every status had zero omissions, and complete-metadata searches found no claim-specific compact receipt item. Full live pm-nilh metadata and all 19 historical events identify the shipped create/update baseline. The duplicate guard matched that broad feature through shared GitHub #437; this is a distinct claim conformance defect, following the existing separate parity-defect precedent. Reopening the historical feature was tested and would remove its shipped July changelog entry, so retain its historical closure and record the claim-specific scope here. Explicit duplicate acknowledgement applies only to this false-positive broad-feature match. Current isolated no-extension reproduction at 94532b596: create returns 71 bytes with id/status/changed_field_count; claim returns 517 bytes with full item/claimed_by/previous_assignee/forced. Intake only, open and unclaimed.
